questions.question: Which of the following is an agro-based industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sugar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agro-based industries:-**

 
 
• **These are those that use agricultural products as their raw materials to produce a wide range of goods and services. **
 
• These industries play a vital role in the economy, providing employment and income to millions of people, and contributing to food security and export earnings.
 
• Agro-based industries can be further classified into two categories:
 
 
• **Primary agro-based industries**: These industries process agricultural products into basic products, such as flour,** sugar, **and oil. **(Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• **Secondary agro-based industries:** These industries process basic agricultural products into more sophisticated products, such as bread, biscuits, and confectionery.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mineral-based industries:-**

 
 
• **These are industries that use minerals and metals as raw materials to produce finished goods. **
 
• These industries are essential to the global economy, as they provide the materials needed for a wide range of products, from construction materials to electronics.
 
• **Aluminium, iron, steel, and coal are not agro-based industries. They are mineral-based industries, which means that they use minerals as their raw materials.**
 
 
• Aluminium is produced from bauxite ore, which is a mineral.
 
• Iron and steel are produced from iron ore, which is also a mineral.
 
• Coal is a fossil fuel, which is formed from the remains of ancient plants and animals.

questions.question: The number of deaths per thousand persons in a year is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**death rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A mortality rate is the number of deaths during a particular period of time among a particular type or group of people.

 
 
• It is also called the Death Rate, that measured as the number of deaths per thousand persons in a year.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Crude Death Rate: indicates the number of death per 1000 mid-year population.

 
 
• CD R is calculated as:
 
• CDR = D x K divided by P
 
• D = total number of deaths registered during the calendar year
 
• P= total mid-year estimated population or the total population of the middle of the year 
 
• K= a constant usually taken as1,000
 
 

 
• Birth rate:

 
 
• Birth rate can be defined as the total number of live births per 1000 population.
 
• Calculative formula: the calculative formula for birth rate is the total number of live births in a particular area during a specific period divided by the total population of that area in thousands.
 
• Birth rate = (Total number of live birth / Total population of the area) x 1000

questions.question: Which country is the biggest producer of rice?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **China** is the **biggest producer** of rice in the world, producing around **146 million metric tons** of rice in **2019.**
 
• **Rice** is a **staple food** in China and is consumed by a large population.
 
• It is also** exported** to other countries.
 
• **Russia **is **not **a major producer of rice as it has a **cold climate **and rice cultivation is **not feasible **there.
 
• **Brazil **is a major producer of crops like **soybean, corn, and coffee**, but it is not a major producer of rice.
 
• **Bangladesh** is a significant producer of rice, but its production is **much lower** than China.
 
• Bangladesh produced around **35 million metric tons **of rice in **2019.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice** is the **staple food** for more than **half of the world's population.**
 
• Other major rice-producing countries include** India, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Thailand.**
 
• **Russia** is a major producer of **wheat, barley,** and other grains.
 
• **Brazil** is the largest producer of** coffee **in the world and is also a major producer of **soybeans, corn, and sugar.**
 
• **Bangladesh** is a densely populated country and** rice** is the **staple food **there.
 
• Hence, the statement "The correct answer is** option 2 (China)"** is correct.

questions.question: Density of population, is expressed as ___________ .

options.text: number of rural persons per unit area
number of literate persons per unit area
number of persons per unit area
number of animals and persons per unit area

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** number of persons per unit area.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Density of population:-**

 
 
• It​ is the **number of individuals **or inhabitants **per unit area.**
 
• It is usually expressed in terms of **persons per square kilometer **or **square mile.**
 
• The density of population is an important indicator of the **level of development and growth** of a particular region or country.
 
• It helps in assessing the availability of **resources, infrastructure, and services** for the people living in that area.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Number of rural persons per unit area:-

 
 
• It is **not an accurate measure** of population density as it only considers the rural population and **excludes urban areas.**
 
 
 
• Number of literate persons per unit area:-
 
 
• It is also **not an accurate measure **of population density as it only considers the literate population and **excludes illiterate individuals.**
 
 
 
• **Number of animals and persons per unit area:-**
 
 
• It is **not an appropriate measure **of population density as it combines two different types of populations and does not provide an **accurate representation of human population density.**

questions.question: Which is the most common ore of oxidised mercury that occurs in granular crusts or veins associated with volcanic activity and hot springs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cinnabar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cinnabar** is the most common ore of oxidised **mercury **that occurs in granular crusts or veins associated with volcanic activity and hot springs.
 
• Cinnabar is a bright red mineral consisting of **mercury sulfide (HgS)**.
 
• It has been used historically as a pigment and is the primary source of mercury.
 
• The mineral forms in a variety of geological environments, often in association with volcanic activity and hot springs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mercury** has various industrial applications, including in thermometers, barometers, and other scientific instruments.
 
• **Exposure to mercury** and its compounds can be highly toxic, affecting the nervous system, digestive system, and immune system.
 
• The extraction and processing of cinnabar to produce mercury must be handled with extreme care to prevent environmental contamination and health hazards.
 
• The use of mercury has declined due to its toxicity and the development of safer alternatives.

questions.question: Which is the largest continent in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Asia Continent

__
 
• Asia is the world's largest continent, having an area of 44,444,100 km2. 
 
• It covers about one-third of the total land area of the earth.
 
• The continent lies in the Eastern Hemisphere.
 
• The Tropic of Cancer passes through this continent.
 
• Asia is separated from Europe by the Ural mountains on the west.
 
• It covers 8.8% of the Earth’s total surface area with a population of 4.4 billion which is 60 % of the world’s total population.
 
• It is a continent of contrast in relief, temperature, vegetation, and people also.
 
• Asia is to the east of the Suez Canal, the Ural River, and the Ural Mountains, and south of the Caucasus Mountains and the Caspian and Black Seas.
 
• It is bounded on the east by the Pacific Ocean, on the south by the Indian Ocean, and on the north by the Arctic Ocean.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ab904072eb623bb22811859e3637cde373ee691d2933c926355e34d9da99384.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are seven major continents. These are separated by large water bodies.
 
• These continents are – Asia, Europe, Africa, North America, South America, Australia, and Antarctica.
 
• The greater part of the landmass lies in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• The combined landmass of Europe and Asia is called Eurasia (Europe + Asia).

questions.question: Which continent of the world is referred to as a “Continent, Dedicated to Science”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antarctica.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Antarctica** is referred to as a** "Continent, Dedicated to Science"** due to its** unique environment **and the presence of **numerous scientific research stations.**
 
• The continent is home to the **South Pole Telescope **and the **IceCube Neutrino Observatory**, among other research facilities.
 
• Scientists conduct studies on topics such as** climate change, glaciology, and astrobiology **in Antarctica.
 
• The continent is governed by the** Antarctic Treaty System**, which outlines guidelines for **scientific research and environmental protection.**
 
• Other options, such as **Africa, North America, and Asia**, are not referred to as a "Continent, Dedicated to Science," although they are home to a number of **scientific research institutions **and initiatives.
 
• Hence, the **correct option **for the given question is **option 2, Antarctica.**

questions.question: The number of live births per thousand persons in a year is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** birth rate.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The birth rate is **the number of individuals born in a population in a given amount of time**. The human birth rate is stated as the number of individuals born per year per 1000 in the population. For example, if 35 births occur per year per 1000 individuals, the birth rate is 35.

 
• **The rate of natural increase is the difference between birth and death rates**. 
 
• It measures the degree to which a population is growing.
 
• Since birth and death rates are measured as the number of births (or deaths) occurring per 1,000 population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mortality rate, or death rate,** is **a ****measure of**** the number of deaths (in general, or due to a specific cause) in a particular population, scaled to the size of that population, per unit o****f time**.
 
• **Growth rates** refer to **the percentage change of a specific variable within a specific time period**. For investors, growth rates typically represent the compounded annualized rate of growth of a company's revenues, earnings, dividends, or even macro concepts, such as gross domestic product (GDP) and retail sales
 
• **The fertility rate** at a given age is **the number of children born alive to women of that age during the year as a proportion of the average annual population of women of the same age.**

questions.question: Which state became the first fully organic farming state in 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sikkim** became the** first totally organic state in 2016**, with the **goal** of** protecting the environment**, its delicate **ecosystem**, and** rich biodiversity**, as well as offering a** healthier lifestyle** for its residents.
 
• The declaration was the culmination of a process that started in 2003, the year when it stopped imports of chemical fertilizers into the State.
 
• The state won the prestigious** Future Policy Gold Award from the UN Food and Agriculture (FAO)**, after beating **51** nominations from around the world.** Sikkim Chief Minister Pawan Kumar Chamling** received the coveted award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Organic farming** is a type of agriculture that uses **pesticides made from organic manure and animal or plant waste**. Chemical pesticides and synthetic fertilizers were causing environmental harm, thus this farming began as a response.
 
• **Sikkim**
 
 
• **​It** is part of the** Eastern Himalayas**, is known for its biodiversity, which includes **alpine and subtropical climates**, as well as being home to **Kangchenjunga,** **India's highest peak** and the** world's third-highest peak**.
 
• **Gangtok** is the** capital** and largest city in Sikkim.
 
• Sikkim Chief Minister** Pawan Kumar Chamling's 24.4 years stint (December 1994 to May 2019) **is the **longest** ever term by a chief minister of any Indian state, surpassing **Jyoti Basu's 23 years** in **West Bengal.**
 
• **Cardamom** and** ginger **are the cash crops of Sikkim. 
 
• Sikkim is the **second-largest **cardamom producer state in India after** Kerala.**
 
• The **highest lakes **in India are** Gurudrongmar Lake** and **Cho Lhamo** **Lake**, both in Sikkim.
 
• Sikkim, which makes up **0.5 percent** of India's landmass, has** 84 glaciers**, the **largest number** compared to any other state or union territory.
 
• Only after **Darjeeling, West Bengal,** Sikkim has the **Highest number of Gurkhas** residing in the state and probably in the world.
 
• **Dalle Khorsani**, from Sikkim, is known to be one of the **world's hottest chilies.**
 
• **Current Chief Minister - **Prem Singh Tamang
 
• **Governor - **Ganga Prasad
